clue.text: Quantity provided with some workability?

definitions.note: an adverb: in a supple manner

blocks.note: first meaning: a stock or amount made available
second meaning: the adverb from supple, said with a different vowel sound

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: SUP-LIE for the stock, SUP-LEE for the adverb formed from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply is an amount provided, while supply as an adverb means flexibly, in a pliant way.

clue.text: Ignored, crossword writer expressed frustration, audibly?

indicators.note: audibly tells us to go by what the phrase sounds like when spoken, not how it is written

blocks.note: a crossword writer is a setter, and expressing frustration with a breath is sighing

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler, frustrated that their puzzle was overlooked, lets out an audible sigh.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something aside is to put it out of consideration, so ignored matches the past participle.

clue.text: Boy that's hurting with cat stuck up tree!

indicators.note: in a down entry, stuck up means placed above the rest, so this part comes first

blocks.note: an informal word for a cat
a boy's name, short for William
the cry someone gives when it hurts

explanation.surface: A boy in pain after a cat has climbed a tree and got stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: The pussy willow is a willow species known for its soft furry catkins in spring.

clue.text: Piece of meat, one in lengthy cut

indicators.note: a cut word is trimmed short, here losing its final letter
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: lengthy means long
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A butcher describing a long cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: LONG loses its G to give LON, and I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Loin is a cut of meat taken from either side of an animal's backbone.

clue.text: Massive rock star with ode I composed

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge rock star who has written a poem himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Massive rock reads like a famous musician; it is a literal lump of rock in space.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a large rocky body orbiting the sun, a giant rock in space.

clue.text: Son leaving a mess, charming chap!

definitions.note: charming in the sense of casting a spell

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the preceding word's letters come out disordered

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
taken as written

explanation.surface: A parent sighs at a son who leaves a mess, but he's such a charmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' looks like going away, but it is just the letters to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali, the hypnotist in Du Maurier's novel Trilby, names someone who controls others by mesmerising them, so a charmer in the spell-casting sense.

clue.text: Ground or aircrew apprehending old environmental activist

indicators.note: apprehending means arresting and holding, so one piece is taken inside the other
ground means crushed up, so the letters are broken and reformed

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Ground staff or aircrew detain an elderly protester at an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: Ground reads as airport ground staff, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An eco-warrior is a campaigner who takes direct action to protect the natural world.

clue.text: Blade decapitates fly

indicators.note: decapitating removes the head, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: to fly high is to soar

explanation.surface: A blade swats a fly, cutting off its head.
explanation.walkthrough: The fly is a verb, not an insect: SOAR loses its S.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of an oar is called the blade, and blade is used by rowers for the oar itself.

clue.text: Administering drug, animal jabbed by something sharp

indicators.note: being jabbed by something means it is stuck into you, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a dog is an animal
a pin is a sharp object

explanation.surface: A vet sedating an animal with a needle.
explanation.definitionFit: Doping is giving someone a drug, especially to sedate them or improve performance.

clue.text: Rock bagged by WAG, a teenager

indicators.note: bagged by means held inside, so the word is concealed within the letters that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A footballer's partner, still a teenager, with a big gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: A WAG is the wife or girlfriend of a footballer, in British tabloid slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded variety of the mineral chalcedony, a semiprecious stone.

clue.text: I appreciate that smart trial at vineyard, say?

blocks.note: ta is an informal British thank-you
to smart is to sting with pain

explanation.surface: A sharply dressed visitor thanking hosts for a trial at a vineyard.
explanation.walkthrough: Smart looks like an adjective for stylish; it is the verb meaning to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine tasting is a sampling session, a trial of wines where they are made.

clue.text: Journey of narcissist, for example, incitement of riot by president, initially

indicators.note: incitement stirs things up, so the following word's letters are stirred
initially points at the opening letter only

blocks.note: e.g. abbreviates for example
taken as written
the first letter

explanation.surface: A vain leader's behaviour, such as stirring up a riot, is all about himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity pursued to boost one's own self-importance, the self-indulgence of a narcissist.

clue.text: Infernal river, backwater did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks us to go by the sound of a word as spoken

blocks.note: the sticks is an informal term for remote rural places

explanation.surface: Someone mishears a river in Hades as a quiet country backwater.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Styx is the river of the underworld, so infernal in the literal sense.

clue.text: Antagonist's surprising lack of activity

indicators.note: something surprising is unexpected, signalling letters that turn up in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An opponent who unexpectedly does nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for is, linking wordplay to definition rather than a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is a state of no flow or development, of standing still.

clue.text: Digit redefining shifts divided by ten

indicators.note: shifts means moves about, so the letters change position
something divided by another is split with it in the middle

blocks.note: taken as written
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Arithmetic jargon: a digit shifts as you divide by ten.
explanation.walkthrough: Digit and divided by ten point to maths, but digit is a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a finger or toe, and the index finger is the forefinger used for pointing.

clue.text: Just wild bears, alone

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run free into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Simply wild bears, on their own in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Just reads as merely, but here it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and reasonable are synonyms for fair, sensible and in keeping with what is right.

clue.text: Something in golf bag, one for the road?

blocks.note: first meaning: a club used for long tee shots
second meaning: a person at the wheel of a vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: One for the road is the idiom for a last drink, which a motorist should refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a golf club for long shots and a person who steers a car.

clue.text: State getting rid of Al, suspiciously

indicators.note: suspiciously suggests something fishy or off, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A US state shady about expelling a gangster such as Al Capone.
explanation.definitionFit: Florida is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the far south-east.

clue.text: Extreme torment: remove locks?

blocks.note: first meaning: great suffering or anguish
second meaning, whimsical: un-tress, as DIS- undoes a word and tresses are locks of hair

explanation.walkthrough: Locks are hair rather than door fastenings; the question mark flags the invented sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is acute physical or mental suffering, and the made-up verb would mean to cut off tresses of hair.

clue.text: Priest ultimately managed month in part of church

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: the last letter
to run something is to manage it
the short form of September

explanation.surface: A priest who finally ran a church project for a month.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of a cross-shaped church, crossing the nave.

clue.text: Fake wine in company

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
PLC, public limited company, is the British abbreviation for a listed company

explanation.surface: A firm selling counterfeit wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic as an adjective describes something artificial or insincere, as in a plastic smile.

clue.text: A hex or an illusion for con artist

indicators.note: an illusion is a deceptive appearance, so the letters are not what they seem and must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A trickster's stock in trade: a curse or a magic trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoaxer tricks people with deliberate deceptions, much as a con artist does.

clue.text: King, dark chesspiece

blocks.note: K is the chess notation for king
dark as a noun, as in after dark, means night

explanation.surface: Two chess pieces: a king and a black piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Dark looks like the colour of a chess piece; it is the noun for nighttime.
explanation.definitionFit: The knight is the chess piece that moves in an L shape.

clue.text: Fit heel on sturdy boot

indicators.note: the heel is the back end, so only the last letter is taken

blocks.note: fit means healthy, or well
the last letter

explanation.surface: Instructions for attaching a heel to a solid boot.
explanation.walkthrough: A welly, short for wellington, is the British word for a rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A welly is a waterproof rubber boot, the everyday British short form of wellington.

clue.text: Sometimes present linked with past?

blocks.note: the present is now
and links two things
the past is then

explanation.surface: A musing on whether the present is connected to the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Now and then is an idiom meaning occasionally, from time to time.

clue.text: Constellation during evening I see, looking to the west

indicators.note: during means within a span, so the word lies inside the letters that follow
in an across entry, facing west means reading right to left

blocks.note: the letters at the join of the three words

explanation.surface: Stargazing at dusk, looking west to spot a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sign of the zodiac is named for a constellation, so the two can stand for each other.

clue.text: Continent in Africa is actually going the wrong way!

indicators.note: in tells us the word sits within the letters that follow
going the wrong way means reading backwards

blocks.note: the letters at the join of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone discovers they are on the wrong continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Africa looks like a candidate answer, being a continent, but the answer is concealed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the earth's continents.

clue.text: I'm going to have bargain discussed?

indicators.note: discussed means talked about, so the word is judged by its spoken sound

blocks.note: a bargain is a good buy

explanation.surface: A shopper planning to haggle over a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodbye is the word of parting, said when someone leaves.

clue.text: Eggs missing head of star

indicators.note: missing its head means the first letter is lost

blocks.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A celebrity chef short of the eggs for a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Head of star looks like the letter S; instead the star is a NOVA, which loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the plural of ovum, the Latin word for an egg cell.

clue.text: Bow found in street for pasta dish

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to bow is to bend or sag under weight
a lane is a small street

explanation.surface: A bow-tie pasta discovered in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow suggests a bow or bow-tie pasta; here it is the verb meaning to bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian baked dish of flat pasta sheets layered with sauce.

clue.text: Cross at server breaking down

indicators.note: something breaking down falls apart, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An office worker annoyed when the computer server crashes.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like the adjective for angry; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across, so it matches the verb to cross.

clue.text: Avian raptor that's cuckoo!

definitions.note: an adjective defining a noun, fair because dictionaries also list avian as a noun meaning a bird

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go haywire into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird of prey that turns out to be a cuckoo: a bird mix-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuckoo looks like a third bird; it means mad here.
explanation.definitionFit: Avian, used as a noun, means a bird, and a parrot is a bird.
